notes.decision: 'The Calling and the Hearing' — the standard Manichaean technical pair (Call from Living Spirit, Answer/Hearing from First Man). Capitalized as personified emanations. The phrase ⲡⲧⲟⲩ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲥⲛⲉⲩ in line 4 ('the five and the two') confirms these are the two divinities added to the five elements to make seven.
Translated 'dwell' as a qualitative/durative form of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand, dwell.' The repeated form (lines 2 and 5) describes the seven elements/spirits as inhabiting their cosmic source.
'They are one' — Lyc. ⲟⲩⲗⲁⲧⲉ likely = ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'one, single, alone' with -ⲁⲧⲉ ending. The First Man and Living Spirit constituting a single unity at this register.

Tentatively 'his struggle/contest.' The form ⲡⲉϩ- (Lyc. possessive 'his') + ⲱⲗⲏⲛ; the root is uncertain. Possibly Greek-derived (πόλεμος?) but the -ⲡ- is missing. Could also relate to a verbal noun of bearing/carrying. Context (the Enemy in line 13, releasing of captives) supports a combat/struggle sense.

'The hidden chamber/repository' tentatively. Compound ⲙⲁ- ('place') + uncertain element. Modified by ⲉⲧⲍⲏⲡ 'which is hidden.' May designate a cosmic storehouse or hidden region; possibly relating to ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ϩⲱⲡ.

Translated 'Fathers' — Lyc. plural of ⲉⲓⲱⲧ/ⲓⲱⲧ 'father.' The chapter that follows (lines 25-end) systematically identifies each major divine emanation (Father of Lights, Mother of Life, Third Ambassador, Beloved of Lights, First Man) as the 'beginning' (ⲁⲣⲭⲏ) of a class of gifts/blessings/counsels/honors. 'Fathers of the Light who are joined to one another' captures this genealogical-emanative system. Alternative reading 'eyes' (= ⲃⲁⲗ) is less coherent with the chapter's content.
'Joined to one another' — qualitative form, possibly from ⲱⲃⲁ/ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'mix, attach.' In the genealogical-emanative reading, the Fathers are 'joined' (linked in succession) rather than 'mixed.'
Lyc. ⲱⲱⲡⲉ = ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become.' The construction is a polite imperative: 'become (in the state of) you knowing' = 'be it known to you.' Mani addressing his disciples.

'The foremost of the Holy Spirit' — apposition identifying the Mother of Life with the highest emanation associated with the Holy Spirit. ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ here means 'the first/foremost one' (substantive) rather than the title 'First Man.'

'Watchers and hunters' — ⲛⲟ̄ⲉⲣⲉⲟ̄ⲉ tentatively from ⲟⲩⲣⲏ/ⲱⲣϫ̄ 'guard, watcher' (Lyc. plural with vowel reduplication); ⲕⲩⲛⲏⲅⲟⲥ = Greek κυνηγός 'hunter.' The pairing of guards/hunters as classes whose 'beginning' is the First Man fits the Manichaean cosmological hierarchy.
